text:
The Senators traded their captain and got better. With Brady Tkachuk now on Florida's top line, Ottawa is 17-7-3 and 7-1-2 over its last ten, and Wednesday's loss in Sunrise, with both Tkachuks on the other bench, ended a winning streak for Linus Ullmark rather than any sense that this team misses its old identity.

Our numbers like how they are doing it. Ottawa gets 55% of the expected goals at five on five, and its goals at both ends match its chances almost to the decimal, so there is very little luck in this record. The depth is the engine. Claude Giroux, Michael Amadio and Ridly Greig have 73% of the expected goals as a line, the best mark of any regular trio in this batch, and Greig keeps drawing penalties (Ottawa draws more than five a game). Tim Stutzle, Dylan Cozens and Fabian Zetterlund have 66%, and Thomas Chabot with Jordan Spence is plus 12 in goals.

There are two things to watch. Stutzle left a game this week after a hard collision with the goalpost, and he has been the best player on the team. And the power play has not yet scored twice in any game this season, after doing it 15 times last year, per Graeme Nichols of Coming Down the Pipe, citing the team's game notes.

Our numbers give Travis Green's team a 94% chance at the playoffs. What we'd watch: whether Ullmark keeps the net with the backup question still hanging around.
